title: Open every issue complete, through one tool (intake)

milestone.title: Workflow · M1: Global GitHub workflow
milestone.description: Every repository gets its labels from one file, issues open complete through one tool, and the guard refuses the shortcut. Done when G2 to G4 are on main.

body:
Global development workflow, step G3, decisions 18, 19, 21 and 25. Agents open issues with a bare `gh issue create`, which skips the template, the labels, the milestone and every board field. All 17 issues opened on 2026-10-22 came out that way.

## What changes

- **The workflow configuration** in this repository: which board each repository belongs to, and the exceptions every workflow tool skips. Private, because it names private repositories.
- **The issue tool,** a command any agent runs. It opens an issue with the repository's form filled in, its `type:` and `scope:` labels, its milestone, its parent and blocked-by links, and every board field (Status, Priority, Size, Estimate, Iteration), on the repository's own board.
- **It refuses a repository with no board mapping,** saying how to add one.
- **It puts that repository's stray issues on its board** whenever it runs, which covers issues opened in the browser.

## Done when

An issue opened with the tool arrives complete on its repository's board, an unmapped repository is refused with the fix named, a stray issue in the repository is added to its board on the next run, and Claude's review passes.

## Scope update, 2026-10-25

The issue's life now has stages with owners (Global development workflow decisions 31 to 33), so this issue covers **intake only**, the tool's `open` command:

- An agent writes a small file describing the issue, and `open` checks it against the repository's form, read from the `.github` repository at run time, before anything is sent.
- The issue lands in **Backlog with no Priority or Size**. Setting those is triage, which is mine as product owner, so whoever opens an issue doesn't choose its priority.
- The rest stands: labels, milestone, parent and blocked-by links, the board mapping, refusing an unmapped repository, and putting the repository's stray issues on its board.

The Definition of Ready gate, the `ready` command, is its own issue.
